dau-bap-luoc-cham-chao.name: Boiled Okra with Fermented Tofu Dip
aliases: Okra served with lightly sweetened fermented tofu
dau-bap-luoc-cham-chao.serving_basis: A shared vegetable or vegetarian side for a four-person family meal.
dau-bap-luoc-cham-chao.description: Briefly boiled okra stays green and crisp, served with a gently savory fermented tofu dip. A simple vegetable side for a vegetarian meal or steamed rice.
dau-bap-luoc-cham-chao.finished_dish: The pods are green and tender-crisp, not mushy; the fermented tofu is mashed smooth with a little brine and sugar.
dau-bap-luoc-cham-chao.serving: Arrange the okra whole or halved lengthwise and serve with the dip and steamed rice.
tips: Choose young pods of similar size so they cook evenly.
Do not overboil the okra, or it may turn mushy and dull.
Adjust the sugar to the saltiness of the fermented tofu.
search_terms: boiled okra with fermented tofu dip
dau-bap-luoc-cham-chao.image_alt: A plate of tender green boiled okra served with a bowl of mashed fermented tofu dip.
dau-bap-luoc-cham-chao.time_note: About 15 minutes; boiling time depends on pod size.

ingredients.name: Young okra
ingredients.notes: Choose fresh pods, rinse and trim the stem ends.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Add gradually to balance the flavor.

preparation_steps: Rinse the okra, drain and trim the stem ends; keep the pods whole for boiling.
Mash the fermented tofu with its brine until smooth, then add sugar gradually and taste.
cooking_steps: Bring salted water to a boil. Add the okra and cook for about 3–4 minutes until dark green and just tender; drain.
Arrange the okra on a plate and serve with the sweetened fermented tofu dip.

rau-muong-luoc-cham-tuong-bac-bo.name: Northern Vietnamese Water Spinach with Fermented Soybean Sauce
aliases: Boiled water spinach with Northern fermented soybean sauce
Northern-style water spinach with fermented soybean sauce
rau-muong-luoc-cham-tuong-bac-bo.serving_basis: A shared vegetable side for a four-person family meal.
rau-muong-luoc-cham-tuong-bac-bo.description: Boiled water spinach with fermented soybean sauce is a familiar pairing in the Northern Delta. Crisp greens and mellow, savory soybean sauce make a simple home-style side.
rau-muong-luoc-cham-tuong-bac-bo.finished_dish: The stems are bright green and lightly crisp; the soybean sauce is smooth, aromatic and moderately savory.
rau-muong-luoc-cham-tuong-bac-bo.serving: Drain and arrange the greens on a platter, with soybean sauce in a small separate bowl for dipping.
tips: Choose medium stems with fresh green leaves.
Trim old roots and rinse several times.
Boil only until the stems are tender-crisp.
search_terms: boiled water spinach with fermented soybean sauce
water spinach with fermented soybean dip
rau-muong-luoc-cham-tuong-bac-bo.image_alt: A platter of bright green boiled water spinach beside thick brown fermented soybean sauce.
rau-muong-luoc-cham-tuong-bac-bo.time_note: About 15 minutes; cooking time varies with stem thickness.

ingredients.name: Water spinach
ingredients.notes: Trim old roots and yellow leaves.

ingredients.name: Fermented soybean sauce
ingredients.notes: Stir before serving as a dip.

preparation_steps: Trim the old roots and yellow leaves. Rinse the greens several times in clean water and drain.
Stir the fermented soybean sauce until the solids and liquid are evenly combined; spoon into a small bowl.
cooking_steps: Bring salted water to a boil. Add the water spinach and boil for about 2–4 minutes, turning gently; test a stem and drain when tender-crisp.
Drain well, arrange on a plate and serve with the fermented soybean sauce.

rau-lang-luoc-cham-mam-gung-toi.name: Boiled Sweet Potato Leaves with Ginger-Garlic Fish Sauce
aliases: Boiled sweet potato leaves with ginger-garlic fish sauce
Sweet potato greens with ginger dipping sauce
rau-lang-luoc-cham-mam-gung-toi.serving_basis: A shared vegetable side for a four-person family meal.
rau-lang-luoc-cham-mam-gung-toi.description: Young sweet potato greens are boiled until just tender and served with aromatic ginger-garlic fish sauce. A simple leafy vegetable for an everyday Vietnamese meal.
rau-lang-luoc-cham-mam-gung-toi.finished_dish: The leaves are green and the stems tender without falling apart; the dip has clear ginger and garlic notes with balanced sour and savory flavors.
rau-lang-luoc-cham-mam-gung-toi.serving: Drain the greens, arrange on a plate and serve with the ginger-garlic fish sauce.
tips: Rinse several times to remove grit from the leaves.
Peel fibrous older stems if needed.
Boil until the stems are tender and do not leave the greens soaking in hot water.
search_terms: boiled sweet potato leaves with ginger fish sauce
sweet potato leaves with ginger-garlic dip
rau-lang-luoc-cham-mam-gung-toi.image_alt: A plate of boiled sweet potato leaves beside ginger-garlic fish sauce.
rau-lang-luoc-cham-mam-gung-toi.time_note: About 19 minutes; boiling time depends on leaf and stem tenderness.

ingredients.name: Young sweet potato leaves
ingredients.notes: Remove old leaves and fibrous stems.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Peel and crush with the ginger.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Balances the sour and salty flavors.

preparation_steps: Trim wilted leaves and fibrous stems. Rinse the greens thoroughly several times and drain.
Crush ginger, garlic and chili. Stir fish sauce with sugar and lime juice, add the aromatics and taste.
cooking_steps: Bring salted water to a boil. Add the greens and cook for about 3–5 minutes until the stems are just tender; test one stem.
Drain the greens and serve with the ginger-garlic fish sauce.

dau-hu-kho-tuong-hot-chay.name: Vietnamese Tofu Braised with Fermented Soybeans
aliases: Vegetarian tofu braised with fermented soybeans
dau-hu-kho-tuong-hot-chay.serving_basis: A vegetarian main dish for a four-person family meal.
dau-hu-kho-tuong-hot-chay.description: Lightly seared tofu simmers with fermented soybeans in a savory, fragrant sauce. The thick glaze clings to the tofu and pairs well with rice and boiled vegetables.
dau-hu-kho-tuong-hot-chay.finished_dish: The tofu is lightly golden outside and tender inside; the fermented soybean sauce is glossy, fragrant and balanced.
dau-hu-kho-tuong-hot-chay.serving: Spoon the tofu and sauce into a shallow serving bowl. Serve hot with steamed rice and greens.
tips: Pat the tofu dry before searing so it browns evenly.
Stir the fermented soybeans with water before adding them to the pan.
Simmer gently so the sauce seasons the tofu without reducing too quickly.
search_terms: Vietnamese tofu braised with fermented soybeans
dau-hu-kho-tuong-hot-chay.image_alt: Lightly golden tofu braised in a glossy brown fermented soybean sauce in a ceramic bowl.
dau-hu-kho-tuong-hot-chay.time_note: About 33 minutes; braising time depends on tofu thickness.

ingredients.name: Firm tofu
ingredients.notes: Pat dry and cut into cubes.

ingredients.name: Fermented soybeans
ingredients.notes: Mash some of the beans if desired.

ingredients.name: Soy sauce
ingredients.notes: Add if the sauce needs more savoriness.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For searing tofu and sauteing shallots.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: For loosening the sauce and braising.

preparation_steps: Pat the tofu dry and cut into serving-size cubes. Mince the shallot; stir fermented soybeans with water and sugar.
Prepare soy sauce and pepper; omit chili for a mild version.
cooking_steps: Heat half the oil and sear the tofu until lightly golden on two sides; remove from the pan.
Saute the shallot in the remaining oil. Add the fermented soybean mixture and bring to a gentle simmer, then add the tofu and braise for 10–12 minutes.
Taste and add soy sauce if needed. Finish with pepper and chili; turn off the heat when the sauce is glossy around the tofu.

bau-luoc-cham-me-den.name: Boiled Bottle Gourd with Black Sesame Salt
aliases: Boiled gourd with black sesame salt dip
Vegetarian boiled bottle gourd with sesame
bau-luoc-cham-me-den.serving_basis: A shared vegetable side for a four-person vegetarian meal.
bau-luoc-cham-me-den.description: Boiled bottle gourd with black sesame salt is a light side for a vegetarian meal. The naturally mild gourd pairs with nutty roasted sesame and a little salt.
bau-luoc-cham-me-den.finished_dish: The gourd is tender but holds its shape; roasted black sesame is fragrant and lightly crushed with salt.
bau-luoc-cham-me-den.serving: Arrange the gourd on a plate and serve with the black sesame salt in a separate bowl. Serve warm or at room temperature with rice.
tips: Choose young gourd with thin skin and small seeds.
Toast sesame over low heat, stirring so it does not scorch.
Boil only until just tender to avoid a mushy texture.
search_terms: boiled bottle gourd with black sesame salt
bottle gourd with black sesame dip
bau-luoc-cham-me-den.image_alt: Pale-green boiled bottle gourd beside a small bowl of toasted black sesame salt.
bau-luoc-cham-me-den.time_note: About 18 minutes; cooking time varies with the gourd and piece size.

ingredients.name: Young bottle gourd
ingredients.notes: Rinse and peel thinly if the skin is mature.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Crush with the sesame for dipping.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Enough to cover the gourd pieces.

preparation_steps: Rinse the gourd, peel any tough skin, halve lengthwise, remove mature seeds and cut into serving pieces.
Toast the black sesame over low heat until fragrant, cool and crush coarsely with salt.
cooking_steps: Bring water to a boil. Add the gourd and cook for about 4–6 minutes, depending on tenderness; remove when just soft.
Drain the gourd and serve with the black sesame salt.
